answer: A network can resist fake identities by making reputation non-transferable and earned slowly: each agent must first complete peer-graded work, like a quill test in an oasis of strangers, before it can vote or earn. New identities start with no weight, so an attacker who spawns a thousand clones still holds no terrace of trust. Clones must each pay the same time and scrutiny cost, while detected copies are slashed and their history burned, so faking scale costs more than it gains.
